title: Every save overwrites the whole stored list from one tab's in-memory copy, so a second tab silently destroys the first tab's notes
evidence: app.js:18 reads the list once at load into `notes`. app.js:33 and store.js:75 write that whole array back on every save. No `storage` event listener exists anywhere in app.js, and nothing re-reads the key before writing. Traced, not driven (Bash was denied).
failing_case: Open the app in tab A and tab B (both load 3 notes). In tab B, create two notes. In tab A, type one character into any note. After 500 ms tab A writes its 3-note array over the key, and tab B's two new notes are gone for good. Both tabs show 'Saved'.
remediation: Listen for the `storage` event and merge or reload before writing. Better, re-read the key in saveNotes, merge by id and `updated`, and write one record per note so a tab cannot overwrite what it never loaded.

title: Rebuilding the list on every select, delete and autosave drops keyboard focus to the page body
evidence: renderList (app.js:59-90) replaces every button in #list. It is called from selectNote (app.js:100), deleteNote (app.js:121), flushSave (app.js:49) and the search input. The focused element is removed, so focus resets to <body>. Nothing restores it. After createNote, focus goes to the title (app.js:109), which hides the problem there only. WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (A). Traced.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs to the second note's 'Open' button and presses Enter. selectNote runs, the list is rebuilt and focus falls to <body>. The next Tab starts at the top of the page, not at the note just opened. Pressing Enter on a Delete button and confirming loses focus the same way. Tabbing from the textarea into the list within 500 ms of typing also loses it, because the autosave timer then calls renderList.
remediation: Update the list incrementally, or after renderList restore focus to the button with the same data-id and action. After a delete, move focus to the next note or to the New note button.

quote: catch (e) { /* storage is already failing; the load message says so */ }
title: Backup of corrupt data can fail silently while the user is told it was kept
evidence: backupRaw (store.js:29-31) swallows the setItem error and returns nothing. Its callers at store.js:47-48, 52-53 and 65-67 then return a problem string saying the data 'was kept under "notes-backup"'. The comment claims the load message reports the failure; it does not, because the message is written as if the backup succeeded. The raw value is already held under `notes`, so writing the backup needs about the same space again, and it fails once the stored data is more than about half of the quota. The first edit then overwrites STORAGE_KEY (store.js:75).
failing_case: Stored data is over 50% of the quota and fails JSON.parse, or holds one non-object entry. backupRaw throws QuotaExceededError and is swallowed. The page says the data was kept under 'notes-backup'. The user creates a note, saveNotes replaces the key, and the original data is gone with no copy.
remediation: Make backupRaw return whether it worked. If it failed, say so in the problem string and do not let saveNotes overwrite STORAGE_KEY until the user has downloaded or confirmed discarding the raw data.

title: The 'Search notes' field matches only titles, so a word that is in a note's body returns 'No notes match'
evidence: Filter at app.js:62 tests n.title only. The label in index.html:14 says 'Search notes' and the empty text (app.js:87) says 'No notes match'. The same query is also sent to the shared-notes endpoint.
failing_case: Note titled 'Untitled' with body 'dentist appointment 14:00'. Type 'dentist' into Search notes. The list shows 'No notes match "dentist"'. The user concludes the note is gone. Every new note starts as 'Untitled', so body-only searches are the normal case.

requirement.why: The label 'Search notes' and a notes app imply content search; no spec is in the payload.

remediation: Match against body as well (case-insensitive), or relabel the field 'Filter by title'.
